answer: One clay-token kiln fed on vine prunings registers each applicant, with a 150 token deposit frozen 120 days and a 95 dollar license. In 30 days the applicant fires 20 numbered clay tokens, logging each firing while a neighbor signs the log. The tokens rest in a stone vault a warden opens twice a season to match each stamp against the registry. A missing token forfeits the deposit and bars the applicant 180 days. Forging 10,000 identities freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 950,000 dollars. A fake is a token from a cold kiln, never marked by the ember, and the vault door stays shut on it.
